clue.text: Welcomes colouring in a drop of ice

parts.note: to welcome someone is to hail them
a tone is a shade or colouring

explanation.surface: Someone greets a bit of tinted ice with enthusiasm.
explanation.definitionFit: A pellet of frozen rain falling from a storm cloud is exactly a small drop of ice.

clue.text: Deep opening appears under house: get out quick!

indicators.note: in a down answer the second piece sits beneath the first

parts.note: a pit is a deep hole in the ground

explanation.surface: A deep hole has opened beneath a house, so flee!
explanation.definitionFit: 'Hop it' is British slang ordering someone to go away at once.

clue.text: Being unprepared, I am having soldiers brought back with temporary housing

parts.note: I am contracts to I'm

indicators.note: housing means holding within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: provisional means temporary

indicators.note: brought back means the soldiers' letters are read in the other direction

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's reserve soldiers

explanation.surface: Caught off guard, someone has troops returned with makeshift accommodation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' looks like a mere link, but 'with temporary housing' means the provisional word holds the reversed soldiers ('brought back'). The TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: Improvisational work is made up on the spot, done without preparation.

clue.text: He scandalised the educational establishment

parts.note: reads as a reformer shocking teachers, but describes the dramatist who wrote The School for Scandal, putting scandal into a school

explanation.walkthrough: The 18th-century Irish playwright wrote The School for Scandal, so he literally gave a school scandal.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard Brinsley Sheridan wrote The School for Scandal, the play that set scandal in a school.

clue.text: Unopened wine is acceptable

indicators.note: something unopened has lost its opening, so the first letter goes

parts.note: Tokay is a sweet Hungarian wine

explanation.surface: A bottle of wine left sealed is fine.
explanation.definitionFit: Okay means satisfactory or all right, a synonym for acceptable.

clue.text: University department needs further painting

parts.note: extra means further, additional
a mural is a painting on a wall

explanation.surface: An academic faculty wants more artwork on its walls.
explanation.definitionFit: An extramural department runs courses for students beyond the university's own walls.

clue.text: Fine fabric found in transport leaving Cumbrian town

indicators.note: the transport word departs from the town's name, so its letters are removed

parts.note: Carlisle is the county town of Cumbria in north-west England
a car is a means of transport

explanation.surface: A delicate cloth turns up in a vehicle driving away from a northern English town.
explanation.walkthrough: CARLISLE is the main town of Cumbria, a county in north-west England; take CAR away and the cotton thread is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Lisle is a smooth, tightly twisted cotton thread used for stockings, hence a fine fabric.

clue.text: General's method is to obtain room for manoeuvre

parts.note: Robert E. Lee was the Confederate general; the 's stands for 'is'
a way is a method

explanation.surface: A commander's strategy aims to win space to move troops.
explanation.definitionFit: Leeway is extra freedom or margin to act, originally a ship's sideways drift.

clue.text: Deliberate deception artfully masks error in MOD

indicators.note: done artfully means cleverly rearranged, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A cunning hoax disguises a blunder at the Ministry of Defence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'artfully' rearranges MASKS ERROR IN MOD. The MOD is Britain's Ministry of Defence.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes illusions meant to obscure the truth, as a conjuror uses them.

clue.text: Withdrew special edition by court journalist

parts.note: an extra is a special edition of a newspaper
ED, short for editor, is a journalist

explanation.surface: A special paper issue about a court reporter was pulled.
explanation.definitionFit: Extracted means pulled out or took out, the same as withdrew.

clue.text: Seeded, working on deliveries? Almost a winner

parts.note: fruit that has been seeded has had its pips removed, so it is pipped
someone handling the mail could be said to be employed at the post office, at the post

explanation.surface: A tournament seed who moonlights as a postman nearly wins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seeded' suggests a tennis ranking, but here it means having had the pips (seeds) taken out.
explanation.definitionFit: To be beaten narrowly at the finishing line is to come agonisingly close to victory.

clue.text: Parallel subject absorbing Head of Research

indicators.note: the subject word soaks up another letter, so it is placed inside

parts.note: a topic is a subject of discussion

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A matching theme takes in the leader of a research team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'absorbing' puts R, the first letter of Research (signalled by 'Head of'), inside TOPIC.
explanation.definitionFit: The tropics of Cancer and Capricorn are lines of latitude, which are called parallels.

clue.text: An orchestra shortly captivated by goddess's exotic dance

indicators.note: being captivated is being held, so these letters sit inside the goddess

parts.note: Hera is the Greek queen of the gods
an becomes the article A

indicators.note: a word cut short loses its final letter

parts.note: a band is a group of musicians, an orchestra

explanation.surface: Some musicians are charmed by a deity's foreign dance routine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortly' trims the band's last letter and 'captivated by' sets the result inside the goddess; Hera was queen of the Greek gods, wife of Zeus.
explanation.definitionFit: The habanera is a slow Cuban dance in duple time, exotic to European ears.

clue.text: Poet advising "Give up the booze"

definitions.meaning: John ... was an English poet and playwright
telling someone to swap alcohol for something from the tap

explanation.definitionFit: John Drinkwater was a Georgian poet, and his surname read as two words urges sobriety.

clue.text: Gallant Greek character by being brave lacks nothing

parts.note: chi is a letter of the Greek alphabet

indicators.note: lacking something means going without it, so a letter is taken out

parts.note: valorous means brave
nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: A courageous Greek is fearless and wants for nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacks' removes O (nothing) from VALOROUS to leave VALROUS. 'character' is a letter of an alphabet, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: Gallant and chivalrous are synonyms describing courteous, brave behaviour, especially towards women.

clue.text: Scams making stacks go in after company books

indicators.note: the stacks are placed following the other pieces

parts.note: NT is the New Testament, books of the Bible
ricks are stacks of hay

explanation.surface: Fraudsters cook a firm's accounts with piles of fake entries.
explanation.walkthrough: NT, the New Testament, is a standard crossword sense of 'books'.
explanation.definitionFit: Con tricks are swindles carried out by confidence tricksters, so scams.

clue.text: Shorebird's to strike back

definitions.note: the apostrophe-s stands for 'is', linking the definition to the wordplay

indicators.note: back says the word for striking is read in the other direction

parts.note: to tonk is to hit hard, a strike

explanation.surface: A coastal bird is about to hit back.
explanation.walkthrough: TONK is informal British for hit hard, especially in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: The knot is a stocky wading bird of sandy coasts and estuaries.

clue.text: Mavis negotiated short let

indicators.note: negotiated suggests these letters are worked round into a new order

explanation.surface: A woman called Mavis haggled over a brief lease.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mavis' looks like a woman's name but is an old word for the song thrush; 'negotiated' rearranges SHORT LET.
explanation.definitionFit: Mavis and throstle are both old or poetic names for the song thrush.

clue.text: Close tight

definitions.meaning: close means nearby, not far off
tight means stingy, mean with money

explanation.definitionFit: Near means close in distance, and in an old sense mean or tight-fisted with money.

clue.text: Never sounded special fun, having company — departed

indicators.note: special indicates the letters of the word fun are put in an unusual arrangement

parts.note: a person at home is receiving visitors, having company
D is the abbreviation for died, departed, in genealogies

explanation.surface: A party full of guests is new territory for someone who has just left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'special' rearranges FUN to UNF. Being AT HOME is an old-fashioned way of saying you are receiving guests.
explanation.definitionFit: To sound water is to measure its depth in fathoms, so an unmeasured depth is unfathomed.

clue.text: Borneo's new king

indicators.note: new indicates the letters are made into a fresh arrangement

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: An island gains a recently crowned monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges BORNEO; the 's is a link meaning 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Oberon is king of the fairies in Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream.

clue.text: Young Guides having unattainable hopes

definitions.meaning: the youngest section of the UK Girlguiding movement
dreams that can never be reached, like the end of an arc of colour in the sky

explanation.definitionFit: Rainbows are the junior branch of Girlguiding, and chasing a rainbow means pursuing an impossible dream.

clue.text: Writer contributing to epic on radio

indicators.note: contributing to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An author takes part in a broadcast saga.
explanation.definitionFit: Joseph Conrad was the Polish-born novelist who wrote Heart of Darkness.

clue.text: Initially doled out some experimental drug

definitions.text: Initially doled out some experimental drug

indicators.note: initially means take the first letter of each following word

explanation.surface: A trial medicine was handed out in small portions to start with.
explanation.definitionFit: Being dosed is being given measured amounts of a drug, as the whole clue describes.

clue.text: Bottom of pool rising to surface is evil-smelling

indicators.note: the bottom of a down word is its final letter
rising to the surface moves that letter up to the top

parts.note: a lido is an open-air public swimming pool

explanation.surface: Sludge from the floor of a swimming pool floats up and stinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bottom of' picks the last letter of LIDO, O, and 'rising to surface' carries it to the start.
explanation.definitionFit: Olid is a rare literary adjective meaning foul-smelling, from Latin olidus.

clue.text: Saluting cartoon, very funny, that's well done

indicators.note: something very funny is crazy, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Someone salutes a hilarious cartoon for being well made.
explanation.walkthrough: 'very funny' rearranges the fifteen letters of SALUTING CARTOON.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying 'well done!' to someone is offering them praise for an achievement.

clue.text: Sage has farewell cut short

indicators.note: cutting short removes the last letter

parts.note: so long is a casual farewell

explanation.surface: A wise person's goodbye is brief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut short' drops the final G from SO LONG.
explanation.definitionFit: Solon was the Athenian lawmaker counted among the Seven Sages, so his name means a wise man.

clue.text: Changed habits and made amends

definitions.meaning: habits as clothes: dressed again in different garments

explanation.definitionFit: Read as re-dressed it means put on fresh clothes; as one word it means put right or compensated for.
